newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: S. Korean investment in E. Europe tops Japan. [CORRECTED 17:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: S. Korean investment in E. Europe tops Japan. [CORRECTED 17:20 GMT]

text.p: South Korean manufacturers surpass their Japanese counterparts as the most active East Asian investors in the central and east European transition economies, the United Nations said in a report on Tuesday.

Investment by South Korean companies in central Europe, the Russian Federation and Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) was a cumulative $705 million at the end of 1995 out of a total of $11.7 billion worldwide, the U.N. Economic Commission for Europe (ECE) said. (Corrects regional figure to $705 million out of a total worldwide figure of $11.7 billion).
"...in the long run, the outlook for cooperation between the Asia-Pacific and the transition economies is bright," it said.
The Geneva-based agency reported the trend in its autumn issue of East-West Investment News issued on Tuesday, but gave no comparative figures for Japanese foreign direct investment.
"(South) Korean manufacturers are the most active East Asian investors in the central and east European transition economies; they are more active than Japanese manufacturers at the moment.
"Among the big conglomerates from Korea, Daewoo is the most active investor in the transition economies, especially in the automotive sectors in Poland, Romania and Uzbekistan," it added.

South Korea became the biggest foreign investor in Poland this year with Daewoo Motor's planned three-year investment of $1.1 billion in FSO (Fabryka Samochodow Osobowych or Factory of Passenger Cars) in Warsaw, according to ECE.

Korean transnationals are increasingly present in Romania, the Czech Republic, Hungary, the Russian Federation, and Uzbekistan where Daewoo Corp. will invest $2.5 billion by the year 2010 to build up its telecommunications networks, it said.
